papers.title: From business intelligence to conservation intelligence: Operationalizing adaptive pest control of crown‐of‐thorns starfish to protect the resilience of the Great Barrier Reef
papers.authors: Samuel A. Matthews, Roger Beeden, Mary C. Bonin, Camille Mellin, Morgan Stuart Pratchett
papers.abstract: Abstract Resilience‐based management (RBM)—which focuses explicitly on preserving and actively enhancing an ecosystem's capacity to resist and recover from cumulative disturbances under climate change—is crucial for enhancing outcomes in conservation interventions as the climate changes. To be effective it requires continuous modeling, assessment, evaluation and adjustment. Here, we deploy enterprise Business Intelligence software for the purpose of conservation (i.e., Conservation Intelligence) to provide the near real‐time analytics and decision support system necessary for effective RBM. This approach is demonstrated using the Crown‐of‐Thorns Starfish Control Program on Australia's Great Barrier Reef where integrated visual dashboards were developed to assess outbreak severity, prioritize control actions, evaluate effectiveness and incorporate emerging research to close the research‐implementation gap. The flexibility of Business Intelligence software allows these Conservation Intelligence tools to be built and maintained “in‐house,” meeting the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority's (GBRMPA) explicit needs and reducing dependency on external developers or researchers. papers.title: Detection of field parasitism of the invasive spotted lanternfly (Lycorma delicatula) by native North American wasps using molecular tools
papers.authors: Yunke Wu, Hannah J. Broadley, Caroline E. Davock, Megan E. Doner, Brian E. Silva
papers.abstract: Abstract The management of invasive pest species frequently involves biological control to suppress the expanding pest populations. Although introduced natural enemies have been favored, the role of native fauna should not be overlooked. The spotted lanternfly ( Lycorma delicatula White; Hemiptera: Fulgoridae) is an invasive, polyphagous plant pest that has rapidly spread across eastern USA over the past decade. Biological control efforts of this pest largely focus on imported parasitoids, but there is increasing evidence of native wasps attacking spotted lanternfly eggs in the USA. To obtain a more accurate estimate of parasitism by one native wasp, Anastatus reduvii (Howard) (Hymenoptera: Eupelmidae), we developed a duplex real-time PCR (qPCR) assay capable of detecting A. reduvii DNA in spotted lanternfly eggs. In silico analysis and non-target testing using three additional Anastatus spp. and five potential host species indicated a low likelihood of false positive amplification. We applied the qPCR assay to spotted lanternfly eggs with parasitoid emergence holes collected from 11 locations in southeastern Pennsylvania, USA that encompass over 6000 km 2 . papers.title: Evaluation of Gallery Injection for Management of Invasive Shothole Borers ( Euwallacea spp.) Associated with Fusarium Dieback in High-Value Trees
papers.authors: Beatriz E. Nobua-Behrmann, John N. Kabashima
papers.abstract: Abstract Invasive shothole borers ( Euwallacea spp.)(ISHB) and their associated fungal pathogens cause substantial damage to urban and riparian trees, creating a need for diverse management approaches to accommodate different infestation scenarios. Gallery injection, a technique in which small volumes of pesticide are delivered directly into active beetle galleries, has not previously been evaluated for ISHB and may provide a localized treatment option that limits pesticide applications to infested portions of the host. The objective of this study was to evaluate gallery injection as a management approach for ISHB, compare the efficacy of different active ingredients delivered using this method, and quantify the volume of solution that could be delivered into active galleries under field conditions. Field trials were conducted on Platanus spp. in Southern California. Active galleries were verified prior to treatment, and beetle activity was assessed following injections. Gallery injections with emamectin benzoate and imidacloprid significantly reduced gallery activity relative to untreated controls, whereas acephate provided intermediate control. papers.title: Effects of emerald ash borer specific gene silencing using RNA interference on soil communities
papers.authors: Faith Boa
papers.abstract: The emerald ash borer (EAB) (Agrilus planipennis Fairmaire) is an invasive wood- boring beetle from Asia that primarily feeds on ash trees (Fraxinus spp.). Since its invasion of North America, EAB threatens the functional extinction of ash with damages and management costs projected to reach $900 million by 2054. Current management strategies have been insufficient to prevent EAB’s spread, highlighting the need to advance innovative approaches like RNAi, which has demonstrated efficacy against EAB in laboratory and greenhouse trials. Double-stranded RNA targeting heat shock 70-kDa protein (hsp) induces EAB mortality, systematically disperses and persists in planta, and causes no phenotypic effects for several ash-associated insects. We evaluated the environmental and nontarget effects of dsHSP, focusing on soil communities. In laboratory soil incubation assays, dsHSP was recovered up to 8 h post-treatment. Exposure of the collembolan Folsomia candida to dsHSP-treated soil had no effects on adult survival or body length, but increased reproduction. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Wildfire and Fuel Treatments in Utah: A Practical Guide and Outcomes From an Oak-Maple Ecosystem
papers.authors: Annie E. Prescott
papers.source: OpenAlex / Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University)
papers.abstract: Wildfire is a natural part of Utah’s landscapes, but as wildfires become more extreme and communities continue to expand into wildland areas, it is increasingly important to understand how wildfires behave and how their negative effects can be mitigated. One way to reduce wildfire risks and protect life, property, and ecosystem services is through fuel treatments — actions that reduce the amount and arrangement of flammable vegetation through mechanical removal, wildland fire, or other methods. Information on wildfire behavior and fuel treatments is abundant but often scattered, ecosystem-specific and difficult to access. In addition, most research in the Western U.S. has focused on conifer forests, leaving other vegetation types understudied. This research addresses these gaps by summarizing wildfire and fuel treatment information for Utah and examining how fuels treatments and wildfire affect wildlands dominated by Gambel oak and bigtooth maple. Chapter II presents a practical guide to wildfire and fuel management in Utah. papers.authors: Shubham Kumar, Astuti Tiwari, Shubhangi Tripathi, Apoorva Choudhary, Sanjeev Kumar
papers.source: OpenAlex / SARPS Journal of Advanced Research in Plant Science
papers.abstract: Biodiversity conservation is shifting from the paradigm of species protection to the maintenance of ecological, genetic, and functional integrity. Earlier biodiversity research and conservation practice focused on understanding and responding to the drivers of biodiversity loss, e.g., habitat loss, climate change, environmental degradation, invasive species, and overexploitation. This review synthesizes the role of plants in sustaining ecosystems, with an emphasis on genetic conservation, ecological restoration, connectivity, conservation biotechnology, monitoring, and adaptive governance. The current crisis of biodiversity loss affects a million species, threatening their extinction, while plant genetic diversity is also disappearing at an alarming rate. According to the Food and Agriculture Organization’s (FAO) Third Report on the State of the World’s Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, 42% of the plant genetic resources evaluated for taxonomic diversity were no longer present in at least one country. papers.title: A privacy aware lightweight edge intelligent framework for real-time lethal threat interception and risk assessment
papers.authors: Himadri Nath Saha, Utsho Banerjee, Ayush Ghosh, Ebrahim Abdulla Mattar, Pronoya Bhattacharya
papers.abstract: Real-time intelligent surveillance systems require a careful balance between predictive reliability, computational efficiency, energy consumption, inference latency, and privacy preservation. However, existing vision-based approaches often achieve high detection accuracy at the expense of computational complexity, limiting their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. To address this challenge, we propose a privacy-preserving, lightweight edge intelligence framework guided by a multi-objective architectural design methodology that jointly balances accuracy, computational efficiency, energy efficiency, real-time responsiveness, and on-device privacy.​ The proposed framework combines hybrid local-global representation learning with a lightweight multi-scale spatial attention mechanism to enhance the recognition of small and partially occluded lethal threats. A lightweight Temporal Threat Validation Module suppresses transient false alarms through temporal consistency analysis, while a context-aware Threat Assessment Network transforms validated detections into quantitative threat intelligence for priority-based decision-making. papers.title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
papers.authors: Matthew D Helton
papers.source: OpenAlex / UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

papers.authors: Chuanxi Peng, Abdullah Khan, Shixin Zhao, Bin Jiang, Yihui Wang
papers.abstract: The cultivation of premium cigar wrappers demands precise environmental control to achieve the requisite leaf thinness and fine veination. While shading is a recognized practice, the mechanistic basis through which light modulation influences carbon assimilation, carbon allocation, and morphological development remains insufficiently resolved. This two year field study characterizes an integrative physiological framework linking photosynthetic performance, carbohydrate status, carbon metabolism related enzyme activity, and leaf morphological development under different shading regimes. Field experiments were conducted using controlled shading treatments to quantify photosynthetic responses, carbon partitioning patterns, and morphological development in three cultivars. Structural equation modeling was used to resolve direct and indirect pathways linking shading to wrapper quality. Moderate shading (70% light transmittance) optimally balanced wrapper quality and economic yield, photosynthesis, carbohydrates, enzymes and leaf traits. papers.title: Mycotoxin contamination in cereals and oil crops: mycotoxigenic fungi, geographic distribution, and green control strategies
papers.authors: Meng-Meng Yang, Ming-Jun Zhao, Zhuo Du, Xue Meng-yao, Zheng Qu
papers.source: OpenAlex / Mycology&#58 An International Journal on Fungal Biology
papers.abstract: Cereals and oil crops play a critical role in the global food system, providing essential energy and nutrition for a vast population. However, during growth and storage, these crops are susceptible to infection by toxigenic fungi, which subsequently produce mycotoxins, posing serious threats to human and animal health. This review systematically summarizes the common toxigenic fungi and their associated mycotoxins in cereals and oil crops, covering their geographical distribution, toxic effects, and contamination status. Furthermore, the article discusses integrated prevention and control strategies for mycotoxin contamination spanning pre- and post-harvest stages, with a focus on key measures such as breeding, crop rotation, biological control, and novel storage technologies, emphasizing the importance of developing green control techniques. Finally, this review highlights the strategic significance of establishing robust monitoring systems, formulating science-based regulatory policies, and strengthening international cooperation to mitigate the risks of mycotoxin contamination.

papers.title: Changes in species composition 20 years after selection cutting in northern hardwood and mixedwood stands
papers.authors: Simon Bilodeau‐Gauthier, François Guillemette, Steve Bédard
papers.abstract: Temperate forests of northeastern North America provide key ecosystem services but are increasingly affected by multiple stressors, including climate change, biological invasions, pollution, and land-use impacts, potentially altering species composition and thus productivity and sustainability of these forests. This study examined 20-year compositional changes in 233 uneven-aged forest stands subjected to single-tree selection (STS) cutting or left unmanaged, encompassing hardwood and mixedwood stands across southern Quebec, Canada. Analyses were based on species-specific proportions of basal area across three developmental stages: saplings, recruit trees, and pre-existing canopy trees. Results indicated that compositional shifts primarily occurred in younger cohorts (saplings and recruits), while canopy composition remained relatively stable. In hardwood stands, the proportion of sugar maple ( Acer saccharum Marsh.) declined among recruits and saplings, whereas that of American beech ( Fagus grandifolia Ehrh.) increased, indicating a gradual replacement dynamic. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.title: Genome-wide CRISPR screening in Spodoptera frugiperda reveals the determinants of insecticide activation and sensitivity
papers.authors: Huidong Wang, Yueru Ye, Tong Zhang, Bingbing Li, Angela Hayward
papers.abstract: Insecticide resistance poses a growing threat to global human health and food security. Addressing this challenge requires a comprehensive understanding of the molecular determinants that govern insecticide action and insect sensitivity. However, identifying and functionally validating the specific genes - among the tens of thousands present in a typical insect genome - that contribute to insecticide mode of action and resistance remains a major challenge. Here, we present a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screening system in a cell line derived from Spodoptera frugiperda, a highly damaging insect pest, and demonstrate its utility for dissecting the molecular basis of insecticide activity and resistance. We construct a library of 90,759 single guide RNAs (sgRNAs) targeting 14,434 genes and conduct a three-round screen under successively increasing concentrations of the insecticide pyridalyl. This enriches for the cytochrome P450 gene CYP333B4. Subsequent P450 inhibitor assays, gene knockout in S. frugiperda, and ectopic expression in Drosophila melanogaster confirm that members of the CYP333B subfamily are key mediators of pyridalyl activation and serve as potential resistance targets.

papers.abstract: Torque teno viruses (TTVs) are ubiquitous components of the human virome whose replication is tightly regulated by host immunity. While elevated total TTV load has been associated with increased mortality in older adults, the clinical relevance of species-level virome composition remains unclear. We profiled the circulating anellovirome in 251 hospitalized older adults using amplicon-based whole-genome sequencing and investigated associations with frailty, cognitive impairment, mortality, immune remodeling, and epigenetic aging. Reduced TTV species evenness was associated with 1-year mortality ( p = 0.013, FDR = 0.052); however, differences in species composition accounted for less than 1% of the total variance (PERMANOVA: Ružička R 2 = 0.0079, p = 0.021, FDR = 0.035; Bray–Curtis R 2 = 0.0082, p = 0.035, FDR = 0.035), indicating that host-related factors rather than distinct clinical phenotypes primarily shaped the virome. papers.title: Understanding the Neurobiology of Heart Rate Variability: Central, Peripheral, and Developmental Contributions in Rodents
papers.authors: Meyrick Kidwell
papers.source: OpenAlex / Open Access Victoria University of Wellington | Te Herenga Waka (Figshare)
papers.abstract: The study of heart rate variability has grown rapidly in popularity in the age of smart technology, however this growth at the cutting edge has progressed without the necessary foundational understanding of the complexities. Rodent modelling of HRV allows for the experimental testing of underlying mechanisms to build a strong foundation for future studies in HRV, however, current rodent experiments are limited and lacking in methodological consistency. The first chapter of this thesis will provide a theoretical overview of HRV from early foundational concepts, up to the current theoretical models, while providing a strong foundation usable to those new to the field of HRV and experts alike. Chapter two provides a data driven methodology for the study of HRV in rats, from a detailed surgical procedure through to the transparent analysis and reporting of essential parameters. Chapter three examines the contributions of the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system to many of the common parameters of HRV using centrally acting and peripherally isolated pharmacological blockades. papers.abstract: Abstract Wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) is the principal staple crop of Pakistan, with Punjab contributing approximately 75% of the country's total wheat production. Leaf rust ( Puccinia triticina ) and stripe rust ( Puccinia striiformis ) are among the most detrimental diseases affecting wheat yield in the country. This study aimed to assess the influence of temperature and relative humidity on the incidence and severity of both diseases in eight major wheat-producing districts of Punjab during the 2024–2025 cropping season. A field survey was conducted at 20 wheat fields with 160 locations at three critical growth stages of the wheat crop and the survey included the commercially cultivated wheat cultivars Akbar-19, MH-21, and Fareed-06. Disease and climatic data were analyzed using multiple linear regression models. The analysis revealed that temperature was the most influential climatic variable, and Regression coefficients indicated that disease incidence increased by approximately 4.3–12.7 percentage points per 1°C increase depending on district. papers.abstract: Rainfall variability has implications for agricultural planning and water resource management in Nasarawa State, Nigeria. This study examined rainfall trends, interannual variability, and growing-season dynamics over the 27-year period from 1997 to 2023. Monthly rainfall and rainy-day data obtained from the Nigerian Meteorological Agency were used to assess annual rainfall totals, rainy-day counts, rainfall onset and cessation, and length of growing season (LGS). Variability was examined across two subperiods, 1997–2010 and 2011–2023, while trends and statistical significance were assessed using linear regression and Student’s t-test. Mean annual rainfall increased by 95.4 mm in 2011–2023 relative to the mean of 1,189.6 mm recorded in 1997–2010. Mean annual rainy-day counts increased slightly from 177 to 179 days, whereas mean LGS declined from 187 to 186 days. Across the full study period, mean annual rainfall was 1,235.5 mm, with a coefficient of variation of 0.12. papers.abstract: L’article relate la première observation d’Amaranthus tuberculatus en métropole, sur une parcelle expérimentale INRAE. L’espèce est comparée aux autres amarantes historiquement observées en France et en Europe. Des informations sur l’historique de sa propagation, ses préférences écologiques et ses caractéristiques biologiques sont fournies. De par sa forte capacité de production de graines, son caractère dioïque, sa faculté de résistance aux herbicides et son fort potentiel compétitif sur les cultures, une attention accrue est nécessaire pour éviter son installation sur le territoire français.

papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming modern society including animal genetics and breeding which is essential for meeting global nutritional needs in supplying milk, meat, and eggs among the most complete sources of protein and micronutrients. Although animal breeding has a long history of using data-driven prediction methods, the application of modern AI approaches remains at a relatively early stage and shows substantial potential for wide-ranging applications in animal genetics and breeding. This study aims to review the current use of AI tools in livestock species across three major applications of high interest: AI-assisted phenotyping, AI-enabled dissection of complex-trait biology (focusing on AI-assisted GWAS and AI-for-omics), and AI-assisted genomic prediction. In addition, we discussed emerging methods and tools developed in human genetics that are not yet widely adopted in farm animals but may offer translational potential for future livestock studies. papers.authors: Yang Qian, Surinderpal Kaur, Amir Rashad Mustaffa, Su Min
papers.abstract: In the context of modernity, profit-driven and unethical practices, such as artificially increasing beef weight and enhancing its visual freshness to meet consumer expectations, have led some traders to inject water into live cattle. Such practices not only violate animal ethics, undermine animal welfare, and disrupt species ecology but also prompt people to reconsider human–cattle relations in China. This study aims to explore ‘human-cattle relations’ in the Chinese context textually and visually, specifically, to examine the interspecies ethical issues involved in ‘human-cattle relations’ in China. This study draws on a self-compiled corpus of cattle representations in selected Chinese news discourse covering a period of six years (2020–2025) through the lens of the Hallidayan approach, Stibbe’s ecosophy and Kress and van Leeuwen’s visual grammar. A corpus-assisted and qualitative analysis was used to reveal more profound interspecies ethical issues. papers.authors: Reena Dubey, Anne Zaar, Riccardo Zustovi, Kevin Dewitte, Jasper Vlerick
papers.abstract: Abstract Faba bean ( Vicia faba L.) is a high-protein legume suited to Northwestern Europe, yet adoption is hindered by limited winter survival, acute cold events, and seed anti-nutritional factors notably vicine and convicine (VC) that constrain food use despite high protein content. We conducted a two-year, two-season study in Belgium (2022–2024) directly comparing winter versus spring accessions via field phenotyping, intact-seed NIRS (n=343), and standardized breadmaking (10% wheat-flour substitution). Winter accessions experienced pronounced cold stress, exhibited slower photothermal growth, and nonetheless produced higher thousand-kernel weight, whereas spring accessions flowered more synchronously and gained height faster per unit thermal time. Culture and microscopy of symptomatic stems indicated that ≈75% of winter injuries were abiotic cold shock, not pathogen mediated. NIRS accurately predicted protein and VC, revealing exploitable diversity: white-flowered lines tended toward higher protein but elevated VC, while several coloured-flowered lines were low-VC, indicating a path to decouple food safety from protein gain. Between May and August 2022, plant samples were collected from the northern region of Osmaniye, Turkey. Leaves of M. communis L. were used to prepare different extracts. The antimicrobial properties of these extracts were tested against nine bacterial strains using the Kirby–Bauer disk diffusion technique. In addition, their antioxidant potential was evaluated through DPPH free radical scavenging and Fe²⁺ chelation assays. GC-FID analysis described 10 different fatty acids in M. communis L.. The major compounds were linoleic acid (omega-6) (C18:2) with 26.274%, lignoceric acid (C24:0) with 21.961%, nervonic acid (C24:1) with 17.714%, cis-4,7,10,13,16,19-Docosahexaenoic with 11. 941%. papers.title: Radioactive fallout legacy of nuclear tests in soils of the Southern Hemisphere
papers.authors: Aydoğan Avcıoğlu, Gerald P. Dicen, Surya Gupta, Christine Alewell, Olivier Evrard
papers.abstract: Abstract Fallout radionuclide (FRN) archived in soils are key tracers of soil redistribution, sediment dynamics, and associated carbon fluxes, yet their global application is limited by poorly constrained baselines in the Southern Hemisphere. Here, we present the first hemisphere-scale baseline and uncertainty maps of 137 Cs and 239+240 Pu soil inventories. Predictions exhibited lower spatial variability and relative uncertaintyfor 137 Cs across most landscapes, whereas 239+240 Pu showed greater spatial variability and larger relative uncertainty. The reconstructed inventories revealed strong latitudinal and topographic gradients, with the highest predicted fallout occurring in tropical and mountainous regions. We further show, under a standardized hypothetical 50% inventory-loss scenario, that uncertainty in low-inventory regions can propagate nonlinearly into soil erosion and carbon-budget estimates, producing carbon budget biases of up to 19.8 t C ha −1 . papers.abstract: A survey conducted in vegetable production areas of the Hevsel Gardens (Diyarbakır, Türkiye) during 2019-2020 determined the occurrence and distribution of root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.). Fifty vegetable production plots were surveyed, 5-10 plants root samples were collected from each plot, and a total of 455 plant samples were evaluated. Galled roots were assessed using a root-galling scale. Species identification was based on the examination of perineal pattern preparations obtained from females under a light microscope and comparison with diagnostic keys. To support morphological identification, esterase isozyme phenotype (EST-PAGE) was performed, and banding patterns were compared with reference phenotypes. Both methods identified the detected root-knot nematodes as Meloidogyne javanica, M. incognita, and M. arenaria. Based on the 22 PAGE-confirmed populations, the prevalence rates of these species were 63.6%, 22.7%, and 13.6%, respectively. Of the 50 plots examined, 22 (44.0%) were infested with root-knot nematodes. Root-knot nematodes were detected in 203 of the 219 plant samples collected from the infested plots, representing a plant-sample infestation rate of 92.7%

papers.abstract: Solitary-phase Oedaleus asiaticus (Bei-Bienko) can switch to the far more destructive gregarious phase as population density rises, posing a serious threat to agriculture, animal husbandry and local economies. The current investigation assessed how developmental stages and population density impacted phase transitions and which genes served as key regulatory elements of this process. The results showed that the younger nymphs were, the higher proportion that shifted from solitary to gregarious phase, whereas adults never switched; a density of 60 insects produced the highest transition rate, whereas lower or higher densities resulted in fewer gregarious individuals. The gregarious locusts maintained their original physical characteristics when they were grown in solitary conditions. Transcriptome analysis showed that gregarious individuals exhibited strong gene expression increases which included the juvenile-hormone acid methyl-transferase gene ( JHAMT ) and the phenylalanine hydroxylase gene ( Hn ) and the DOPA decarboxylase gene ( DDC ) and a chemosensory protein gene ( CSP ). papers.title: Organic Amendments for Simultaneous Soil Carbon Sequestration and Soil-Borne Pathogen Suppression: Mechanisms and Perspectives
papers.authors: Qudrat Ullah, Esha Arshad, Kainat Fatima, Waqas Haider, Muhammad Qasim
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of soil science and plant nutrition
papers.abstract: The depletion of soil organic carbon (SOC) and the escalating prevalence of soil-borne plant pathogens represent critical challenges to terrestrial biogeochemical stability and global food security. With approximately 24% of terrestrial carbon reserves lost and over US$220 billion in annual crop losses attributed to soil-borne diseases, understanding biotic and geochemical controls on soil health is essential. This review evaluates the dual functionality of organic amendments (agricultural residues, animal manures, and urban biosolids) as drivers of simultaneous carbon restoration and pathogen suppression. We analyze the mechanisms governing these benefits, focusing on the biogeochemical coupling of element cycles and microbiome-mediated processes such as the formation of recalcitrant carbon, organo-mineral protection, and microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE). Biochar applications can increase SOC stocks by 26–33% (11.5–14.6 Mg ha⁻¹), while silicon-modified biochar reduces the bacterial wilt index caused by Ralstonia solanacearum by 73.4%. Furthermore, we examine the geochemical mechanisms of pathogen suppression through antibiosis, resource competition, and signaling disruption.

papers.abstract: Precise biophysical characterization of non-enveloped viruses and virus-like particles (VLPs) is essential for evaluating assembly, structural integrity, and sample heterogeneity - key parameters that influence infectivity, manufacturability, and therapeutic performance. Analytical ultracentrifugation, light scattering, and mass photometry provide complementary information on particle size distributions, empty/full ratios, and assembly quality. Native and charge-detection mass spectrometry extend this, enabling accurate mass determination and genome-loading assessment. Solution-based structural techniques, such as SAXS and spectroscopy, provide dynamics. High-resolution X-ray crystallography, cryogenic electron microscopy, and tomography reveal global architectures, quaternary arrangements, and conformational switching essential for entry and maturation. Besides these methods, atomic force microscopy also allows nanoscale visualization in conjunction with mechanical profiling, linking physical stability with functional behavior. papers.title: Viral infections as gatekeepers of bacterial infections in otitis media: Immune mechanisms and implications for therapeutic interventions
papers.authors: Ayesha Zahid, Hazrat Ismail, Jennifer C. Wilson, Irwin Darren Grice
papers.abstract: Otitis media (OM) is a highly prevalent inflammatory disease of the human middle ear and a key contributor to poor health outcomes in young children on a global scale. While bacterial pathogens such as Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Moraxella catarrhalis are well-recognised contributors to OM, increasing evidence highlights respiratory viruses as critical gatekeepers that predispose the middle ear to bacterial infection. Viral upper respiratory infections initiate mucosal inflammation, disrupt epithelial barrier integrity and mucociliary clearance, and alter host immunological responses. Collectively, these changes create a permissive environment for bacterial colonization, ascension, and persistence within the middle ear. Viral and bacterial coinfections are commonly found and are linked to poorer clinical outcomes, extended inflammation, and increased disease severity. This review synthesises current evidence on the mechanisms by which viruses prime the middle ear for subsequent bacterial infections, with particular emphasis on epithelial dysfunction, receptor modulation, interferon-driven immune responses, and alterations in innate immune training. papers.title: CSLB4 modulates primary cell wall architecture and resistance to Brevicoryne brassicae in Arabidopsis thaliana
papers.authors: Felipe Moraga, Daniela Arias-G, Dayán Sanhueza, Joaquín Delgado-Rioseco, Isabel Fuenzalida‐Valdivia
papers.abstract: The plant cell wall (CW) is a key determinant of plant defense; however, the extent to which natural variation in primary CW architecture contributes to resistance against phloem-feeding insects remains unclear. Here, we combined genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with functional analyses to identify genetic determinants of resistance against the specialist aphid Brevicoryne brassicae in Arabidopsis thaliana. GWAS identified a significant locus on chromosome 2 associated with aphid performance. Integration of haplotype and epidermis-specific expression data prioritized CSLB4, a member of the cellulose synthase-like B family. Loss-of-function analysis using two independent T-DNA insertion alleles reduced B. brassicae offspring by 39-56%, indicating enhanced resistance, whereas performance of the generalist aphid Myzus persicae was unaffected. papers.title: GFR-SAM: Training-Free Referring Camouflaged Object Segmentation via Cross-Image Prompting
papers.authors: Yilong Yang, Jianxin Tian, Shengchuan Zhang, Liujuan Cao
papers.source: OpenAlex / ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
papers.abstract: Referring Camouflaged Object Detection (Ref-COD) requires segmenting hidden targets guided by reference cues. While supervised methods are annotation-heavy and training-free approaches via sparse point-prompting are sensitive to localization errors, we propose GFR-SAM, a robust three-stage training-free framework. GFR-SAM shifts the paradigm from fragile point-matching to a "Generate-Filter-Refine" pipeline. First, we introduce In-Context Exemplar-guided Segmentation, empowering SAM3 with cross-image inference to generate candidate masks via holistic visual exemplars, bypassing its native intra-image constraints. Second, a Region-Global Contrastive Filtering module ranks candidates through DINOv3-based prototypical alignment, effectively suppressing background distractors. Finally, a Geometric-Semantic Refinement module synergizes bounding box and text prompts to recover fine-grained boundaries and enhance instance recall. Evaluated on the R2C7K benchmark, GFR-SAM outperforms existing training-free methods by 8.7% in weighted F-measure (F ? w ) and competes with supervised state-of-the-art counterparts. papers.title: From detection to decision: molecular, genomic, and AI innovations for managing Ganoderma boninense in oil palm
papers.authors: Qudrat Ullah, Waqas Haider, Farhang Hameed Awlqadr, Ahmed Bilal, Muhammad Tayyab Arshad
papers.abstract: Ganoderma boninense causes basal stem rot (BSR) in oil palm, resulting in substantial economic losses, particularly for smallholders who contribute approximately 40% of global production. This review synthesizes advances in molecular diagnostic techniques (qPCR, LAMP), whole-genome sequencing of resistant Elaeis guineensis genotypes, and AI-driven remote sensing to enhance understanding of G. boninense pathobiology. Soilborne mycelia of the pathogen can persist for more than 10 y. Asymptomatic infections, which are frequently missed by conventional methods, can lead to significant disease spread within plantations over 2 y. CRISPR-based paper-strip tests have demonstrated high sensitivity (detecting < 1 pg DNA in laboratory settings), while marker-assisted selection has helped identify additional resistance QTLs. Trichoderma biofilms and biodegradable fumigants reduced soil inoculum by 50–75% in controlled studies. AI-based decision support systems have demonstrated promising accuracy for guiding interventions and potential cost savings, although further field validation across diverse conditions is needed.

Results The results showed that bacterial community dynamics were significantly influenced by compartment and disease stage.
